1→# DuckDB Data Agent
     2→
     3→> **Note:** This project is built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code)(using Opus 4.6 and [superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)) by more than 95% and human-reviewed by author.
     4→
     5→[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy)
     6→
     7→A SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. Upload CSV files, write SQL queries, or ask questions in plain English — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend.
     8→
     9→## Features
    10→
    11→### SQL Playground
    12→
    13→- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
    14→- **CSV file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV files (up to 500 MB) with automatic schema detection
    15→- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
    16→- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
    17→- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
    18→- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
    19→- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types
    20→
    21→### AI Agent
    22→
    23→- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
    24→- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
    25→- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
    26→- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
    27→- **Edit & delete messages** — Hover over any user message to edit or delete it; editing re-sends the modified query with prior conversation as context, deleting rewinds the conversation to that point
    28→- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and key are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API
    29→- **Langfuse observability** (optional) — Built-in [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) tracing for monitoring agent interactions, with a one-click dashboard link in the UI
    30→
    31→## Getting Started
    32→
    33→### Prerequisites
    34→
    35→- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
    36→- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
    37→- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)
    38→
    39→### Installation
    40→
    41→```bash
    42→make install
    43→```
    44→
    45→Or install frontend and backend separately:
    46→
    47→```bash
    48→cd frontend && npm install
    49→cd backend && poetry install
    50→```
    51→
    52→### Configuration
    53→
    54→Copy the example environment file and add your Anthropic API key:
    55→
    56→```bash
    57→cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
    58→```
    59→
    60→Edit `backend/.env` and set your key:
    61→
    62→```
    63→ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
    64→ANTHROPIC_MODEL=sonnet    # optional, defaults to sonnet
    65→```
    66→
    67→> Both variables are only needed for the AI agent. The SQL playground works without them, but both require the backend running.
    68→
    69→#### Langfuse (optional)
    70→
    71→To enable agent tracing with [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/), add these to `backend/.env`:
    72→
    73→```
    74→LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...
    75→LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...
    76→LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com   # optional, defaults to cloud
    77→```
    78→
    79→When configured, every agent conversation is traced (LLM turns, tool calls, SQL execution) and a **Langfuse Traces** button appears in the agent panel header linking to your dashboard. When not configured, tracing is disabled with zero overhead.
    80→
    81→### Development
    82→
    83→Start both the frontend and backend:
    84→
    85→```bash
    86→make dev
    87→```
    88→
    89→Or run them separately:
    90→
    91→```bash
    92→make frontend   # http://localhost:5173
    93→make backend    # http://localhost:8000
    94→```
    95→
    96→Open http://localhost:5173 to use the app. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` requests to the backend automatically.
    97→
    98→## Production Build and Deployment
    99→
   100→The project ships as a single Docker image that bundles the React frontend and FastAPI backend. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` builds the frontend, then copies the output into the backend's static directory.
   101→
   102→### Build and run locally
   103→
   104→```bash
   105→docker build -t duckdb-data-agent .
   106→docker run -p 10000:10000 \
   107→  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... \
   108→  -e LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... \
   109→  -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... \
   110→  duckdb-data-agent
   111→```
   112→
   113→Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.
   114→
   115→### Deploy to Render
   116→
   117→A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):
   118→
   119→1. Push this repo to GitHub.
   120→2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
   121→3. Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`). To enable Langfuse tracing, also set `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`.
   122→
   123→Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.
   124→
   125→## Project Structure
   126→
   127→```
   128→├── frontend/               # React frontend
   129→│   ├── public/             #   Static assets (Langfuse icon)
   130→│   ├── src/
   131→│   │   ├── components/     #   UI components (editor, results, sidebar, chat)
   132→│   │   ├── agent/          #   Agent service (SSE event handling)
   133→│   │   ├── AgentContext.tsx #   Agent state management
   134→│   │   └── types.ts        #   Shared TypeScript interfaces
   135→│   ├── index.html          #   HTML entry point
   136→│   ├── package.json        #   npm config
   137→│   └── vite.config.ts      #   Vite bundler config
   138→├── backend/                # FastAPI backend
   139→│   └── app/
   140→│       ├── main.py         #   App setup & CORS
   141→│       ├── config.py       #   Environment variables (API key, model)
   142→│       ├── database.py     #   DuckDB connection & query execution
   143→│       ├── agent.py        #   Agent loop & SSE streaming
   144→│       ├── tracing.py      #   Langfuse client wrapper & initialization
   145→│       ├── tools.py        #   Agent SDK tool definitions (execute_sql)
   146→│       ├── data/           #   Sample datasets (titanic.csv)
   147→│       └── routes/         #   API endpoints (tables, query, chat, langfuse status)
   148→├── Dockerfile              # Multi-stage production build
   149→├── render.yaml             # Render deployment config
   150→└── Makefile                # Dev commands (install, dev, clean)
   151→```
   152→
   153→## Tech Stack
   154→
   155→**Frontend**
   156→- [React](https://react.dev/) 18 + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
   157→- [Vite](https://vite.dev/)
   158→
   159→**Backend**
   160→- [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) + [Uvicorn](https://www.uvicorn.org/)
   161→- [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) (Python)
   162→- [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
   163→- [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) (optional, for observability)
   164→
   165→## License
   166→
   167→[MIT](LICENSE.txt)
   168→

    17→    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl && \
    18→    curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash - && \
    19→    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs && \
    20→    apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    21→
    22→# Install Claude CLI globally
    23→RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
    24→
    25→RUN pip install --no-cache-dir poetry && \

    37→RUN useradd -m appuser

1→import duckdb
     2→import os
     3→import tempfile
     4→from typing import Any
     5→
     6→
     7→class Database:
     8→    def __init__(self):
     9→        self.conn = duckdb.connect(":memory:")
    10→
    11→    def execute_query(self, sql: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    12→        """Execute a SQL query and return results as dict with columns, rows, rowCount."""
    13→        result = self.conn.execute(sql)
    14→        if result is None:
    15→            return {"columns": [], "rows": [], "rowCount": 0}
    16→        columns = [desc[0] for desc in result.description] if result.description else []
    17→        rows = [dict(zip(columns, row)) for row in result.fetchall()] if columns else []
    18→        return {"columns": columns, "rows": rows, "rowCount": len(rows)}
    19→
    20→    def load_csv(self, file_bytes: bytes, filename: str, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    21→        """Load a CSV file into a DuckDB table. Returns table info."""
    22→        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".csv", delete=False) as tmp:
    23→            tmp.write(file_bytes)
    24→            tmp_path = tmp.name
    25→        try:
    26→            self.conn.execute(
    27→                f'CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "{table_name}" AS SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto(\'{tmp_path}\')'
    28→            )
    29→        finally:
    30→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
    31→        return self.get_table_info(table_name)
    32→
    33→    def get_table_info(self, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    34→        """Get info about a specific table."""
    35→        cols_result = self.conn.execute(f'DESCRIBE "{table_name}"')
    36→        columns = [
    37→            {"name": row[0], "type": row[1]}
    38→            for row in cols_result.fetchall()
    39→        ]
    40→        count_result = self.conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{table_name}"')
    41→        row_count = count_result.fetchone()[0]
    42→        return {"name": table_name, "columns": columns, "rowCount": row_count}
    43→
    44→    def list_tables(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    45→        """List all tables with their schema info."""
    46→        tables_result = self.conn.execute("SHOW TABLES")
    47→        table_names = [row[0] for row in tables_result.fetchall()]
    48→        return [self.get_table_info(name) for name in table_names]
    49→
    50→    def drop_table(self, table_name: str) -> None:
    51→        """Drop a table."""
    52→        self.conn.execute(f'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "{table_name}"')

    23→def build_system_prompt(conversation_history: list[dict] | None = None) -> str:
    24→    tables = db.list_tables()
    25→    prompt = """You are a helpful data analyst assistant working with a DuckDB database.
    26→You can execute SQL queries using the execute_sql tool to answer questions about the user's data.
    27→
    28→Guidelines:
    29→- Write clear, efficient DuckDB SQL queries
    30→- When exploring data, start with small queries (use LIMIT)
    31→- Explain your findings in plain language after getting results
    32→- If a query fails, try to fix it and retry
    33→- Use double quotes for table and column names that might conflict with reserved words
    34→"""
    35→    if not tables:
    36→        prompt += "\nNo tables are currently loaded. Ask the user to upload a CSV file first."
    37→    else:
    38→        prompt += "\nCurrently loaded tables:\n"
    39→        for table in tables:
    40→            prompt += f'\nTable: "{table["name"]}" ({table["rowCount"]} rows)\nColumns:\n'
    41→            for col in table["columns"]:
    42→                prompt += f'  - "{col["name"]}" ({col["type"]})\n'
    43→
    44→    if conversation_history:
    45→        prompt += "\n\nPrevious conversation (for context, the user is now editing a message):\n"
    46→        for entry in conversation_history:
    47→            role = entry.get("role", "user").capitalize()
    48→            content = entry.get("content", "")
    49→            prompt += f"\n{role}: {content}\n"

    54→def _extract_tool_result_text(content: object) -> str:

    56→    if content is None:
    57→        return ""
    58→    if isinstance(content, str):
    59→        return content
    60→    if isinstance(content, list):
    61→        parts = []
    62→        for item in content:
    63→            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("type") == "text":
    64→                parts.append(item.get("text", ""))

    69→async def stream_chat(
    70→    message: str,
    71→    session_id: str | None = None,

   103→    propagate_ctx = None

   126→        current_text = ""
   127→        has_tool_calls = False

1→"""Utilities for manipulating Claude Agent SDK session JSONL files."""
     2→
     3→import json
     4→import os
     5→import re
     6→import tempfile
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→
     9→from app.config import PROJECT_DIR
    10→
    11→_SESSION_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-f0-9\-]{36}$")
    12→
    13→
    14→def get_session_path(session_id: str) -> Path:
    15→    """Construct the path to a session JSONL file.
    16→
    17→    The Claude Agent SDK stores session files at:
    18→        ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl
    19→
    20→    where <encoded-cwd> replaces "/" with "-" in the current working directory.
    21→    """
    22→    if not _SESSION_ID_PATTERN.match(session_id):
    23→        raise ValueError(f"Invalid session_id format: {session_id}")
    24→    cwd = PROJECT_DIR
    25→    encoded_cwd = cwd.replace("/", "-")
    26→    return Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects" / encoded_cwd / f"{session_id}.jsonl"
    27→
    28→
    29→def _is_user_query(entry: dict) -> bool:
    30→    """Return True if the JSONL entry is an actual user query (not a tool result).
    31→
    32→    User query entries have type "user" with message.content as a string.
    33→    Tool result entries also have type "user" but message.content is a list.
    34→    """
    35→    if entry.get("type") != "user":
    36→        return False
    37→    message = entry.get("message", {})
    38→    content = message.get("content")
    39→    return isinstance(content, str)
    40→
    41→
    42→def truncate_session(session_id: str, user_message_index: int) -> None:
    43→    """Truncate a session JSONL file at the given user message index.
    44→
    45→    Reads the session file, counts user query entries, and truncates the file
    46→    so that all lines from the specified user message onward are removed.
    47→
    48→    Args:
    49→        session_id: The session identifier.
    50→        user_message_index: Zero-based index of the user message at which to
    51→            truncate. All lines from this user message onward are discarded.
    52→
    53→    Raises:
    54→        FileNotFoundError: If the session file does not exist.
    55→        ValueError: If user_message_index is not found in the session.
    56→    """
    57→    session_path = get_session_path(session_id)
    58→
    59→    if not session_path.exists():
    60→        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Session file not found: {session_id}")
    61→
    62→    lines = session_path.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True)
    63→
    64→    truncation_line: int | None = None
    65→    user_count = 0
    66→
    67→    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    68→        stripped = line.strip()
    69→        if not stripped:
    70→            continue
    71→        try:
    72→            entry = json.loads(stripped)
    73→        except json.JSONDecodeError:
    74→            continue
    75→
    76→        if _is_user_query(entry):
    77→            if user_count == user_message_index:
    78→                truncation_line = i
    79→                break
    80→            user_count += 1
    81→
    82→    if truncation_line is None:
    83→        raise ValueError(
    84→            f"User message index {user_message_index} not found in session {session_id}"
    85→        )
    86→
    87→    truncated_content = "".join(lines[:truncation_line])
    88→
    89→    # Atomic write: write to temp file in the same directory, then replace
    90→    dir_path = session_path.parent
    91→    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=dir_path, suffix=".jsonl.tmp")
    92→    try:
    93→        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as tmp_file:
    94→            tmp_file.write(truncated_content)
    95→        os.replace(tmp_path, session_path)
    96→    except BaseException:
    97→        # Clean up temp file on failure
    98→        try:
    99→            os.unlink(tmp_path)
   100→        except OSError:
   101→            pass
   102→        raise
   103→

## Comprehensive Project Overview: DuckDB Data Agent

### Overall Project Structure

The **DuckDB Data Agent** is a full-stack web application combining a React frontend with a FastAPI backend. The total project size is approximately **509MB** (125MB frontend, 302MB backend - primarily due to node_modules and venv).

```
/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/
├── frontend/               # React 18 + TypeScript frontend (125MB)
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── components/     # 20+ React components
│   │   ├── agent/          # Agent service (SSE handling)
│   │   ├── AgentContext.tsx # State management
│   │   ├── App.tsx         # Main app component
│   │   ├── types.ts        # TypeScript interfaces
│   │   ├── useAgent.ts     # Agent hook
│   │   └── main.tsx        # Entry point
│   ├── public/             # Static assets
│   ├── vite.config.ts      # Vite configuration
│   ├── tsconfig.json       # TypeScript config
│   ├── package.json        # npm dependencies
│   └── dist/               # Built output
├── backend/                # FastAPI backend (302MB)
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── main.py         # FastAPI app setup
│   │   ├── config.py       # Environment config
│   │   ├── database.py     # DuckDB wrapper
│   │   ├── agent.py        # Agent loop & streaming
│   │   ├── tools.py        # Tool definitions
│   │   ├── tracing.py      # Langfuse integration
│   │   ├── session.py      # Session management
│   │   ├── routes/         # API endpoints
│   │   │   ├── chat.py
│   │   │   ├── query.py

├── Dockerfile              # Multi-stage Docker build
├── Makefile               # Development commands
├── render.yaml            # Render.com deployment config
└── README.md
```

---

### Tech Stack

#### **Frontend**
- **Framework**: React 18.3.1 with TypeScript 5.6
- **Build Tool**: Vite 5.4.10
- **UI Libraries**:
  - `react-markdown` - For markdown rendering
  - `remark-gfm` - GitHub Flavored Markdown support
- **Linting**: ESLint 9.13 with TypeScript support
- **Transpiler**: SWC (via `@vitejs/plugin-react-swc`)

#### **Backend**
- **Web Framework**: FastAPI 0.129.0 + Uvicorn 0.41.0
- **Database**: DuckDB 1.4.4 (in-process SQL engine)
- **AI/Agent**: Claude Agent SDK 0.1.38
- **Observability**: 
  - Langfuse 3.0.0 (optional tracing)
  - LangSmith with OpenTelemetry support
- **Config**: python-dotenv 1.2.1
- **Package Manager**: Poetry

#### **Deployment**
- **Docker**: Multi-stage build (Node.js 20 → Python 3.12)
- **Hosting**: Render.com (render.yaml included)
- **Python**: 3.12+, Node.js 20+

---

### Backend Source Files (13 Python Files)

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| **main.py** (44 lines) | FastAPI app setup, CORS middleware, route registration, static file serving for SPA |
| **config.py** (15 lines) | Environment variable loading (API key, model selection, Langfuse config) |
| **database.py** (64 lines) | DuckDB connection wrapper with methods for query execution, CSV loading, table listing |
| **agent.py** (249 lines) | Core agent loop; Claude SDK integration; streaming SSE events; thinking blocks; tool execution |
| **tools.py** (37 lines) | `execute_sql` tool definition; MCP server creation for DuckDB access |
| **tracing.py** (90 lines) | Langfuse client initialization; OTel auto-instrumentation for Claude Agent SDK |
| **session.py** (103 lines) | Session file utilities; JSONL file manipulation for conversation history |
| **routes/chat.py** (49 lines) | `/api/chat` and `/api/chat/edit` endpoints; streaming responses |
| **routes/query.py** (22 lines) | `/api/query` endpoint; direct SQL execution with EXPLAIN support |
| **routes/tables.py** (48 lines) | `/api/tables`, `/api/upload`, `/api/upload/sample`, `/api/tables/{name}` DELETE |
| **routes/langfuse_status.py** (14 lines) | `/api/langfuse/status` - returns Langfuse configuration status |
| **routes/__init__.py** | (empty) |
| **app/__init__.py** | (empty) |

---

### Frontend Source Files (18 TypeScript/TSX Files)

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| **App.tsx** (223 lines) | Main app component; mode switching (Agent/Editor); table management; file upload |
| **AgentContext.tsx** (300+ lines) | React Context for global agent state; message management; streaming callbacks |
| **types.ts** (59 lines) | TypeScript interfaces: `ChatMessage`, `TableInfo`, `QueryResult`, `ToolCallResult`, etc. |
| **main.tsx** (11 lines) | React entry point; mounts App to root |
| **useAgent.ts** (6 lines) | Hook to access AgentContext |
| **agent/agentService.ts** (100+ lines) | SSE event handler; `runAgentLoop` and `runAgentEditLoop` functions |
| **components/AgentPanel.tsx** (60 lines) | Chat UI with message display; Langfuse button; clear messages |
| **components/MessageBubble.tsx** (300+ lines) | Individual message rendering; collapsible thinking blocks; edit/delete actions |
| **components/ChatInput.tsx** (45 lines) | Text input for agent queries |
| **components/QueryEditor.tsx** (35 lines) | SQL editor component |
| **components/ResultsTable.tsx** (100+ lines) | Interactive table with sorting, filtering, and column search |
| **components/ResultMarkdown.tsx** (30 lines) | Markdown renderer for EXPLAIN results |
| **components/InlineQueryResult.tsx** (100+ lines) | Inline display of SQL query results in chat |
| **components/Sidebar.tsx** (90 lines) | Table browser; column inspector; delete table functionality |
| **components/FileUpload.tsx** (80 lines) | Drag-and-drop CSV upload; sample data button |
| **components/ErrorMessage.tsx** (20 lines) | Error notification dismissible alert |
| **vite-env.d.ts** | Vite type definitions |
| **App.css**, **index.css** | Global styles and component styles |

---

### Configuration Files

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| **backend/.env.example** | Template for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, Langfuse credentials |
| **frontend/vite.config.ts** | Build config; dev proxy to `/api` → `http://localhost:8000` |
| **frontend/tsconfig.json** | TypeScript config with references to app and node configs |
| **Dockerfile** | 2-stage build: frontend (npm build) → backend (Python + Node.js) |
| **Makefile** | Development commands: `make dev`, `make install`, `make backend`, `make frontend` |
| **render.yaml** | Render.com deployment blueprint; environment variable setup |
| **.gitignore** | Excludes: node_modules, dist, .env, .claude/settings.local.json |

---

### Key Features & Architecture

#### **SQL Playground**
- DuckDB in-process analytical database
- CSV drag-and-drop upload (up to 500MB)
- Sample Titanic dataset included
- SQL query execution with real-time results
- EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE support (rendered as markdown)
- Table browser with schema inspection

#### **AI Agent**
- Claude 3.5 Sonnet (default, configurable)
- Natural language to SQL conversion
- Real-time streaming responses with Server-Sent Events (SSE)
- Visible reasoning/thinking blocks (collapsible)
- Inline query results within conversation
- Edit & delete message history
- Session persistence via JSONL files
- Privacy-focused: API key stored server-side

#### **Observability**
- Optional Langfuse integration for trace monitoring
- OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation
- LangSmith integration for agent spans
- Dashboard link in agent panel header

#### **Development Workflow**
- `make install` - Install all dependencies
- `make dev` - Run frontend + backend concurrently
- `make backend` - Run FastAPI on port 8000
- `make frontend` - Run Vite dev server on port 5173
- Frontend proxies `/api` requests to backend

---

### API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Method | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `/api/health` | GET | Health check |
| `/api/tables` | GET | List all tables with schema |
| `/api/upload` | POST | Upload CSV file |
| `/api/upload/sample` | POST | Load Titanic dataset |
| `/api/tables/{name}` | DELETE | Drop table |
| `/api/query` | POST | Execute SQL directly |
| `/api/chat` | POST | Stream agent response (SSE) |
| `/api/chat/edit` | POST | Edit message with context |
| `/api/langfuse/status` | GET | Check Langfuse config |

---

### Project Statistics
- **Total source/config files**: ~100+ files
- **Python files**: 13
- **TypeScript/TSX files**: 18
- **React Components**: 20+
- **CSS modules**: 10+
- **Lines of code**: ~3,000+ (excluding node_modules, __pycache__)
- **Latest commits**: Focus on edit/delete message features and agent enhancements

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse

from app.routes import tables, query, chat, langfuse_status

app = FastAPI(title="DuckDB Data Agent API")

    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],

)

@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "ok"}


# Serve frontend static files in production
STATIC_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "static"

    app.mount("/assets", StaticFiles(directory=STATIC_DIR / "assets"), name="static-assets")

    @app.get("/{full_path:path}")
    async def serve_frontend(full_path: str):
        """Serve frontend for any non-API route (SPA fallback)."""
        file_path = STATIC_DIR / full_path
        if full_path and file_path.is_file():
            return FileResponse(file_path)
        return FileResponse(STATIC_DIR / "index.html")

import logging

from app.config import LANGFUSE_ENABLED, LANGFUSE_BASE_URL

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_langfuse_client = None


def _init_langfuse():
    """Initialize Langfuse with OTel auto-instrumentation for Claude Agent SDK."""
    global _langfuse_client
    if not LANGFUSE_ENABLED:
        logger.info("Langfuse not configured, tracing disabled")
        return

    # Set OTel env vars so langsmith routes traces through Langfuse.
    # Must be set before any langsmith import to avoid LRU cache issues.
    for key, val in {
        "LANGSMITH_OTEL_ENABLED": "true",
        "LANGSMITH_OTEL_ONLY": "true",
        "LANGSMITH_TRACING": "true",
    }.items():
        os.environ.setdefault(key, val)

    try:
        from langfuse import get_client

        _langfuse_client = get_client()

        if _langfuse_client.auth_check():
            logger.info("Langfuse connected successfully")
        else:
            logger.warning("Langfuse auth check failed, tracing disabled")
            _langfuse_client = None
            return

        # Suppress harmless warnings from langsmith/OTel integration BEFORE
        # creating Client (background thread starts during Client.__init__):
        # 1. "Run compression is not enabled" — race condition: thread starts
        #    before otel_exporter is assigned. Batch processing uses env vars.
        # 2. "Invalid type dict for attribute" — langsmith sets usage_metadata
        #    as a dict, but OTel only accepts primitive types.
        logging.getLogger("langsmith.client").setLevel(logging.ERROR)
        logging.getLogger("opentelemetry.attributes").setLevel(logging.ERROR)

        # Pre-create the global LangSmith Client with otel_enabled=True
        # so the background tracing thread knows to use OTel-only mode.
        from langsmith.client import Client
        from langsmith.run_trees import configure

        configure(client=Client(otel_enabled=True))

        # Enable auto-instrumentation for Claude Agent SDK
        from langsmith.integrations.claude_agent_sdk import configure_claude_agent_sdk

        if configure_claude_agent_sdk():
            logger.info("Claude Agent SDK auto-instrumentation enabled")
        else:
            logger.warning(
                "Failed to configure Claude Agent SDK auto-instrumentation"
            )

    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning("Failed to initialize Langfuse: %s", e)
        _langfuse_client = None


def get_langfuse_client():
    """Return the Langfuse client or None if not configured."""
    return _langfuse_client


def get_langfuse_dashboard_url() -> str | None:
    """Return the Langfuse project traces URL or None."""
    if _langfuse_client is None:
        return None
    try:
        project_id = _langfuse_client._get_project_id()
        if project_id:
            return f"{LANGFUSE_BASE_URL}/project/{project_id}/traces"
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning("Failed to get Langfuse project ID: %s", e)
    return LANGFUSE_BASE_URL


# Initialize on module import
_init_langfuse()

"""Utilities for manipulating Claude Agent SDK session JSONL files."""

import json
import os
import re
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from app.config import PROJECT_DIR

_SESSION_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-f0-9\-]{36}$")


def get_session_path(session_id: str) -> Path:
    """Construct the path to a session JSONL file.

    The Claude Agent SDK stores session files at:
        ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl

    where <encoded-cwd> replaces "/" with "-" in the current working directory.
    """
    if not _SESSION_ID_PATTERN.match(session_id):
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid session_id format: {session_id}")
    cwd = PROJECT_DIR
    encoded_cwd = cwd.replace("/", "-")
    return Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects" / encoded_cwd / f"{session_id}.jsonl"


def _is_user_query(entry: dict) -> bool:
    """Return True if the JSONL entry is an actual user query (not a tool result).

    User query entries have type "user" with message.content as a string.
    Tool result entries also have type "user" but message.content is a list.
    """
    if entry.get("type") != "user":
        return False
    message = entry.get("message", {})
    content = message.get("content")
    return isinstance(content, str)


def truncate_session(session_id: str, user_message_index: int) -> None:
    """Truncate a session JSONL file at the given user message index.

    Reads the session file, counts user query entries, and truncates the file
    so that all lines from the specified user message onward are removed.

    Args:
        session_id: The session identifier.
        user_message_index: Zero-based index of the user message at which to
            truncate. All lines from this user message onward are discarded.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the session file does not exist.
        ValueError: If user_message_index is not found in the session.
    """
    session_path = get_session_path(session_id)

    if not session_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Session file not found: {session_id}")

    lines = session_path.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True)

    truncation_line: int | None = None
    user_count = 0

    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        try:
            entry = json.loads(stripped)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue

        if _is_user_query(entry):
            if user_count == user_message_index:
                truncation_line = i
                break
            user_count += 1

    if truncation_line is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"User message index {user_message_index} not found in session {session_id}"
        )

    truncated_content = "".join(lines[:truncation_line])

    # Atomic write: write to temp file in the same directory, then replace
    dir_path = session_path.parent
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=dir_path, suffix=".jsonl.tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as tmp_file:
            tmp_file.write(truncated_content)
        os.replace(tmp_path, session_path)
    except BaseException:
        # Clean up temp file on failure
        try:
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        except OSError:
            pass
        raise
